Because the package contains electronic equipment, a signature is required. We can try again tomorrow between nine and noon. part4.script: Is the winter weather leaving your skin dry and rough? Then it's time to try Lumera's new Deep Hydration Cream. Developed with skin-care experts, our cream uses natural ingredients like oat extract and shea butter to keep your skin soft all day long. Deep Hydration Cream is available now at pharmacies and department stores nationwide. For a limited time, when you buy a full-size jar, you'll also receive a travel-size bottle of our best-selling face wash at no extra cost. Visit lumera dot com to find a store near you.

part4.speaker: M
part4.script: In local news, the Greenfield Recycling Plant will begin accepting electronic waste next month. Until now, residents who wanted to get rid of old computers, phones, or televisions had to drive more than an hour to the nearest electronics recycling center, in Millbrook. The plant's director, Sandra Okoye, says the change was made possible by a grant from the state environmental agency, which paid for new equipment to safely remove metals and batteries. Residents will be able to drop off items free of charge on the first Saturday of every month. Now, you might be wondering about large appliances like refrigerators. Well, those still won't be accepted. For a full list of items, visit the city's Web site. Coming up after the break, we'll have the weekend weather forecast.

I know some of our regular customers won't be happy about this, so please be polite and explain the reason when it comes up. To help you, I've prepared a short handout with answers to common questions. It's in the staff room, next to the coffee machine. Please read it before your first break today.

part4.script: Welcome to Thornbury Press, and thank you for joining today's tour. For over a hundred years, we've published some of the country's most popular novels and children's books. We'll begin here in the editorial department, where our editors work closely with authors to prepare their manuscripts. Next, we'll visit the design studio, where our book covers are created. Then we'll finish in the archive room, which holds a first edition of every book we've ever printed. Now, I should mention that the archive room is kept quite cold to protect the old paper. I'd also ask you not to take photographs anywhere on the tour, as many of the projects you'll see haven't been announced yet. At the end, each of you will receive a voucher for twenty percent off any purchase at our bookshop.

=== PASSAGE 1: ARTICLE ===
Northvale Recycling Center Expands Into Food Waste
By Marcus Lee

ASHFORD (May 2) — Northvale Recycling Center will begin collecting food waste from apartment complexes in Ashford on June 2, the company announced this week. The program will start as a six-month pilot at three complexes, each with more than 100 units, before being offered to other residential buildings next year.

Participating complexes will receive large green collection bins free of charge, and Northvale trucks will empty them twice a week. Accepted items include fruit and vegetable scraps, coffee grounds, eggshells, and bread. Meat, bones, and dairy products cannot be accepted at this stage because the center's composting equipment is not designed to process them.

The food waste will be turned into compost at Northvale's facility on Quarry Road and sold to farms and garden centers in the region. "Nearly 30 percent of what residents throw away is food," said operations director Gail Simmons. "Composting it instead of sending it to a landfill benefits both the environment and the local economy."

===
=== PASSAGE 2: NOTICE ===
BIRCHWOOD TERRACE — NOTICE TO ALL RESIDENTS

We are pleased to announce that Birchwood Terrace has been selected as one of the three complexes taking part in Northvale Recycling Center's new food-waste pilot program. Beginning in June, green food-waste bins will be placed next to the regular trash containers behind each building.

To help you get started, every household will receive a free countertop container for collecting food scraps in the kitchen. Containers can be picked up at the management office from May 26 to May 30 between 9:00 A.M. and 5:00 P.M.

A representative from Northvale will hold an information session in the community room on May 28 at 7:00 P.M. to explain the program and answer questions.

— Birchwood Terrace Management Office

I'm also planning to attend the information session. Before then, could you tell me whether leftover chicken bones can go in the green bins? I cook chicken often, so this would make a big difference for my household.

Thank you,
